questions.question: You can reduce the risk of hydroplaning by driving:
questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Driving more slowly reduces this risk.

questions.question: A good defensive driver:

options.text: Watches what other drivers are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers are doing.
questions.explanation: A defensive driver watches other drivers and prepares for possible problems. Even experienced drivers get distracted.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should NOT:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Check for other drivers in the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call police about the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call police about the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and use your turn signal. Look for other drivers in the same lane. Do not use your cell phone while driving.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can
Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level greater than 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol reduces your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving will suffer. You cannot drink and drive safely.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Speed up to create more distance.
Brake suddenly to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Watch your mirrors for tailgaters or cars approaching fast. If someone is too close, slow down and let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?
questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, with or without a crosswalk.

questions.question: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes:
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines at intersections and crosswalks. They show drivers exactly where to stop.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, you should:

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes or passing. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency. Change lanes as little as possible. Avoid cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: If a driver sees an animal on the road, they should:

options.text: Pass the animal as closely as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very cautious.
questions.explanation: Be careful when you see an animal on the road. Drive slowly past the animal to avoid scaring it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cars in right lane must slow down.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic are about to become one lane ahead.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive carefully.

questions.question: Highway signs that require drivers to follow an instruction are called:
questions.correctAnswerText: Regulatory signs.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must or must not do. Breaking these rules can result in a penalty.

questions.question: Another driver is passing your car. You should:

options.text: Signal to the other driver when it is safe for them to pass.
Look for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane when another driver passes you on the left. Look for oncoming traffic and slow down to make it easy for them to move back into the right lane.

questions.question: Green arrows on traffic signals control turns from specific lanes. A green arrow means:

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
You can go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You may only proceed if a circular green light is also shown.
It points the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. Traffic in that lane must turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal to slow down before using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to stop in time. Release the gas pedal first, then press the brake gently to slow down smoothly.

questions.question: When another driver is tailgating you:

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane is open, wait for clear road ahead and slow down gradually so they will pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating and a right lane is open, move over. If no right lane exists, wait for clear road and slow down gradually to let them pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the chance of being hit from behind.

questions.question: Using signals before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb:

options.text: Is only necessary if other cars are nearby.
Is required by law and is a safe driving habit.
Is only necessary during the move, not before it.
Is not necessary if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is required by law and is a safe driving habit.
questions.explanation: You must signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. Always signal before pulling away from a curb to tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time:

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to signal they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle arrives to your right at the same time, let them go first. You can proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. You must:

options.text: Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car, try to find the owner. If you cannot, leave a written note that includes your name, address, and details about the accident.

questions.question: What color are highway signs that show the distance to the next exit?
questions.correctAnswerText: Green with white letters
questions.explanation: Information signs showing destinations use green with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: Drivers cannot pass from either side of a ____ centerline.
questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line in the center means no traffic from either direction can cross it to pass.

questions.question: To reduce headlight glare at night, look:

options.text: At the center of the road
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are too bright, look at the right side of the road. Do not look directly at the lights. The glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Merge into the right lane and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Let emergency vehicles pass by immediately moving to the right side of the road and stopping. If you are in an intersection, go through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: An arrow painted on the pavement means:

options.text: Drivers in this lane may make the movement shown if they choose to.
Drivers in this lane must make the movement shown, but only if traffic lights are not working.
Drivers in this lane must stop completely before making the movement shown.
Drivers in this lane must make the movement shown while following traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers in this lane must make the movement shown while following traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow on the pavement tells drivers in that lane to move in the direction shown. Drivers must follow traffic signs and signals before moving in that direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead curves left, then right.
The road ahead curves right, then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road will curve to the right and then to the left. Slow down to safely handle these curves.

questions.question: Driving while distracted:

options.text: Usually slows your reaction time to hazards.
Is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually slows your reaction time to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions delay how quickly you react to traffic and road hazards. Distracted driving is always unsafe.

questions.question: Crossbuck signs show:
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn you to yield to trains at railroad crossings. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass even if it could be dangerous.
Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You can cross them to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the most difficult driving season.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires are a good choice for winter driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control in snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter driving is difficult and requires extra care. Check antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels regularly. Snow tires improve grip on slippery roads.

questions.question: The 'No zone' is:

options.text: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
A roadway with restrictions on stereo volume.
A television show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on the sides, rear, and front. Cars cannot be seen in these areas. These blind spots are called the 'No zone.'
